bottlenecks.reading: What NU supplies is competition and low cost to serve in concentrated, high-fee banking. Banking concentration (HHI 2024-25) is 889 in Brazil, 993 in Mexico, 1,262 in Colombia against 328 in the US, 373 in Germany, 488 in France (NU's own table from BCB, CNBV, SFC, ECB data). NU claims cost to serve and G&A per active customer about 85% below Brazilian incumbents (internal analysis; incumbents have 1,685 to 3,955 branches). This gap does not close quickly because incumbents' branch and legacy-system costs are structural; the counter is that Itau already earns ROE 24.3% at 35.5% efficiency, so incumbents are not fragile.

Mexico is an under-penetrated credit market: 63% of adults have a bank account, about 37% formal credit, 16% a bank credit card (INEGI ENIF 2024 / Dec 2025); top five issuers hold about 85% of card portfolio. NU reached 9.2M credit-card customers in 2025 (+35%), about half with no prior card, and over 5% of card purchase volume (Banxico). The scarce step was the bank license: CNBV gave Nu Mexico its operations authorization on 2026-07-09 (search excerpt of Nu's 6-K of 2026-07-10), which allows full deposit and credit products; Mexico was 6.8% of FY2025 revenue (US$808.1M), loan-to-deposit ratio only 35% in 2Q26. BBVA Mexico (loan growth about 10%) and Mercado Pago (Mexico fintech MAU +45%) add capacity at the same time.

Brazil's public rails lower the barrier for every entrant: Pix reached US$6.3 trillion in 2025 (+29%, 179.7M users), NU originates close to 20% of Pix transfers (BACEN), Inter reports about 9% Pix share (2Q26 filing excerpt). Open Finance and salary portability make switching easier for NU's customers as well as incumbents'. Open rails mean the moat is cost, data and primary-bank engagement, not access.

The scarce thing that limits growth is cheap, well-underwritten funding and credit quality, not demand: NU's 90+ day NPL was 6.9% in 2Q26 (up 35 to 40 bps in the quarter, book +37% FXN to US$39.4B) against Itau 1.9% and Banorte 1.5%, a different, much riskier book (low-income, unsecured). Mercado Pago grows its book +75% (credit cards +91%) and Inter +29%, so competitors are adding capacity in the same unsecured consumer segment.

Hypothesis: regulatory and fiscal policy in Brazil (taxes on financial institutions, interest or payroll-loan rate caps, Selic path) is the largest external swing for NU's margin; the 20-F payroll-loan note says INSS payroll loans are capped against Selic. A search headline of 2026-10-26 to 11-01 reports a 20% one-day NU share fall after a Brazilian election result; not read, cause and content unverified.

notes: fd NAMED COMPETITORS (20-F Item 4, pf_10k_20260408): the filing names no individual competitor in Brazil; it says NU faces 'large incumbent financial institutions, major technology companies, and smaller emerging fintech entrants'. In Mexico it names Banco Azteca, Banorte, Santander Mexico, HSBC and BanCoppel (credit card issuers NU surpassed in new cards) and Sofipos as fintech peers. The competitors list is therefore the analyst's selection by market: ITUB (Brazil incumbent), INTR (Brazil digital bank), MELI/Mercado Pago (Brazil and Mexico), BBVA Mexico and Banorte (Mexico). Bradesco, Banco do Brasil, PicPay, SoFi (US, prefetched peers.json, does not serve NU's customers, dropped) are not recorded: no own-filing numbers were read for them.

fd SHARE Brazil customers: NU 113M at FY2025 (62% of adults 18+; growth above the five largest incumbents combined, BCB per 20-F, pf_10k_20260408) to almost 118M at 2Q26 (fd_nu_2q26), about +4.4% in two quarters. Inter&Co 45.3M clients but 26.4M active (58.3%, fd_inter_2q26) against NU's 83.5% monthly activity rate (86% in Brazil, fd_nu_2q26): NU has about 2.6 times Inter's customers and a higher engagement. Mercado Pago 88M MAU across all countries (+30%, fd_meli_2q26); not comparable one-to-one with NU customers.

fd SHARE profitability: 2Q26 ROE NU 33% (fd_nu_2q26) vs Itau 24.3% (fd_itub_2q26) vs Inter 16.3% (fd_inter_2q26); net income growth yoy NU +49% vs Inter +34% vs Itau +7.8%; MELI operating margin 6.7% in 2Q26 (fd_meli_2q26). NU earns the highest return and grows fastest of the Brazil names, with the highest 90+ NPL (6.9% vs Itau 1.9%).

fd SHARE revenue by geography (pf_10k_20260408): NU Brazil revenue US$8,409.9M (2024) to US$11,038.3M (2025), +31%; Mexico US$523.1M to US$808.1M, +54%; other US$118.1M to US$237.3M. NU 2025 revenue pool share is about 5% of its serviceable market (retail revenue pool US$227.9B across the three countries, NU internal analysis). Against competing revenue over the same period: MELI revenue +39% (FY2025, whole company), ITUB revenue +8.4% (FY2024, BRL, last year in prefetch). Segment-level competing revenue for MELI Brazil/Mexico fintech or Inter Brazil is not read: gap.

fd SHARE Mexico: NU 15.8M customers at 2Q26 (about 15% of adults), over 5% purchase-volume share of cards (Banxico, 20-F), third-largest regulated institution by customers (CNBV). Competing digital growth: Mercado Pago Mexico fintech MAU +45% (fd_meli_2q26, hypothesis that it competes for the same customers); BBVA Mexico profit +12.1% constant FX, loans +9.9% (fd_bbva_2q26, search excerpt). Hypothesis: NU's Mexican growth comes mostly from first-time card users (about 50% had no card), not from taking share from BBVA or Banorte.

fd COMPETITOR TIMING: Q3 2026 results of Itau, Inter, MercadoLibre and Nu (due 2026-11-12) were not out at 2026-11-01; all competitor numbers are 2Q26 (reported 2026-08-05) or FY2025. Itau's 2Q26 EPS missed consensus per a search excerpt (not registered).
